description: Reconciliation operation: sets rfc_message_id for the row matching tenant + provider_message_id, stores generatedRfcMessageId, is a no-op when repeated, keeps the first on-wire id when given a different one, and does not touch another tenant's row with the same provider_message_id.
After reconciliation, the next ticket and comment-thread notification builds In-Reply-To/References from on-wire ids, with no generated id that was replaced left in the chain.

ResendEmailProvider: returns the on-wire id as rfcMessageId when Resend supplies it; returns a successful result with no rfcMessageId when the id is null or the fetch fails; POST /emails is called exactly once in both cases.

Resend webhook: a signed email.sent with message_id reconciles the matching log row; an event without message_id changes nothing; an unsigned event changes nothing; delivered/bounced/complained events still publish their workflow events.

Round trip: a Resend-sent ticket notification followed by an inbound reply with no reply token whose In-Reply-To is the amazonses on-wire id lands on the ticket; the same holds when the reply names the generated id, and when the stored and inbound ids differ only in brackets or domain case.
Backfill: updates resend rows that Resend returns, leaves rows it does not return, and a second run makes no changes.
Existing SMTP SES test for resolveSesOnWireMessageId and its logged rfc_message_id still passes against the shared contract.
